theorem.statement:
For every \(h\in\mathbb N_{+}\), the exact existential-support residual complexity is
\[
 \rho(h)=B_h=\operatorname{Bell}(h).
\]
More precisely, equality partitions \(\pi_i\) are a uniformly exact continuation summary, and for each \(h\) there is one finite binary ordered instance with \(h\) nonfactual retained contexts in which every partition of \(\mathcal H\) occurs at one layer and any two distinct partitions are separated by a common legal future pin specification and a terminal predecessor-normal conjunction \(\gamma^{\circ}\). Acceptance is existential on each side and may use different complete-predecessor response systems \(f\in\mathfrak F\). Consequently there is no uniformly coarser exact state for this residual interface. The single-conjunction compiler \(\mathsf C_1\) retains the upper bound \(B_h3^{(h-1)/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})\); the state lower bound makes no running-time lower-bound claim and no claim about all reduced multi-valued decision diagrams.
theorem.proof_tex:
We use the existential-support equivalence in \texttt{def:residual-minimality-handle}. First, \texttt{thm:partition-continuation} says that two feasible prefixes with the same complete-prefix equality partition have exactly the same attainable support of every later retained-world value-column sequence subject to every later pin. A terminal predecessor-normal conjunction is a finite conjunction of tests on those later values. Thus its acceptance is feasible from the first prefix if and only if the corresponding tested column sequence is in that prefix's support, which holds if and only if it is in the second prefix's support. The completing response systems supplied by the two support statements need not be the same. Hence equality of \(\pi_i\) implies residual equivalence, and there are at most
\[
 |\operatorname{Part}(\mathcal H)|=\operatorname{Bell}(h)=B_h
\]
residual classes in every instance and at every layer. Therefore \(\rho(h)\leq B_h\).

We prove the reverse inequality on a single binary instance for each \(h\). Write \([h]=\{1,\ldots,h\}\) and
\[
 \mathscr C_h=\{C:\varnothing\neq C\subsetneq[h]\}.
\]
Take binary endogenous variables in the order
\[
 S\ \prec\ (Z_C:C\in\mathscr C_h)\ \prec\ Y,
\]
where the selector coordinates are placed in any fixed order. Pin the entire factual path to zero. For each \(j\in[h]\), define the nonfactual intervention
\[
 I_j=\operatorname{do}\!\left(S=1,\ Z_C=1\text{ for every \(C\in\mathscr C_h\) with \(j\in C\)}\right),
\]
leaving every unlisted selector and \(Y\) natural, and put \(\mathcal H=\{I_1,\ldots,I_h\}\). If \(h\geq2\), then \(I_j\neq I_\ell\) for \(j\neq\ell\), because the coordinate \(Z_{\{j\}}\) is intervened on in \(I_j\) and not in \(I_\ell\). For \(h=1\), the sole context is \(I_1=\operatorname{do}(S=1)\). Thus \(|\mathcal H|=h\) in all cases. The factual predecessor begins with \(S=0\), whereas every retained-world predecessor begins with \(S=1\); consequently every factual response row used below is distinct from every retained-world row at the same coordinate.

Let \(m=1+|\mathscr C_h|\), the layer immediately before \(Y\); when \(h=1\), this is the layer just after \(S\). Fix an arbitrary partition \(\alpha\in\operatorname{Part}([h])\). We construct a feasible prefix \(P_\alpha\) through layer \(m\). At \(S\), set the factual natural response to zero; every \(I_j\)-world has value one by intervention. At selector \(Z_C\), set every natural response row reached by a retained world to
\[
 z_C^\alpha=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&C\text{ is a block of \(\alpha\)},\\
 1,&C\text{ is not a block of \(\alpha\)},
 \end{cases}
\]
and set the separately reached factual row to zero. This row prescription is consistent. Indeed, retained worlds with the same complete predecessor tuple receive the same prescribed value \(z_C^\alpha\); retained worlds with different tuples use different complete-predecessor rows; and the factual tuple is different because its \(S\)-coordinate is zero. Assumption~\texttt{ass:complete-predecessor-functions} therefore permits all these assignments, while Assumption~\texttt{ass:finite-alphabets} supplies values for all unused rows.

The resulting selector value in world \(I_j\) is
\[
 E(f,I_j)_{Z_C}=
 \begin{cases}
 1,&j\in C,\\
 z_C^\alpha,&j\notin C.
 \end{cases}
\]
If \(C\) is not a block of \(\alpha\), this value is one for every \(j\). If \(C\) is a block of \(\alpha\), the column is exactly the indicator of membership in \(C\). Hence two indices in the same \(\alpha\)-block agree at every selector. Conversely, if \(j\) and \(\ell\) lie in different \(\alpha\)-blocks and \(A\) is the block containing \(j\), then \(A\in\mathscr C_h\), and the selector \(Z_A\) has values one in world \(I_j\) and zero in world \(I_\ell\). For the one-block partition there is no block in \(\mathscr C_h\), and every selector is constantly one. It follows in every case that
\[
 x^{I_j}_{\leq m}=x^{I_\ell}_{\leq m}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 j\text{ and \(\ell\) belong to the same block of \(\alpha\)}.
\]
Thus \(P_\alpha\) is feasible, respects every factual zero pin, and induces exactly \(\alpha\). Since \(\alpha\) was arbitrary, all \(B_h\) partitions occur at the same layer of this one instance.

It remains to separate them in the corrected residual sense. Let \(\alpha\neq\beta\). If some block of \(\beta\) meets two blocks of \(\alpha\), choose such indices \(j,\ell\), let \(A\) be the \(\alpha\)-block containing \(j\), and define
\[
 b_t=\mathbf 1\{t\notin A\},\qquad t\in[h].
\]
Then \(b\) is constant on every \(\alpha\)-block but is nonconstant on the selected \(\beta\)-block. If no \(\beta\)-block meets two \(\alpha\)-blocks, then \(\beta\) refines \(\alpha\); because they are unequal, some \(\alpha\)-block meets two \(\beta\)-blocks, and the same construction applies after interchanging \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\). Thus, after orienting the pair if necessary, there is always a binary vector \(b\) constant on every block of the first partition and nonconstant on a block of the second.

Use the common future factual pin \(Y=0\) and the terminal conjunction
\[
 \delta_b=\bigwedge_{j=1}^h\{Y_{I_j}=b_j\}.
\]
Every intervention coordinate in \(I_j\) precedes \(Y\), and \(Y\notin\operatorname{dom}(I_j)\). Therefore \texttt{def:query-normalizer} deletes no intervention pair and performs no self-intervention simplification. After canonical sorting, \(\delta_b\) is predecessor-normal. Its distinct retained context set is exactly \(\{I_1,\ldots,I_h\}=\mathcal H\); the factual context \(\varnothing\) is not adjoined because no factual atom occurs in \(\delta_b\).

From \(P_\alpha\), each block \(A'\in\alpha\) supplies one distinct complete predecessor tuple at \(Y\). Because \(b\) is constant on \(A'\), define the corresponding natural row of \(f_Y\) to equal that common bit. Define the factual row to be zero; it is distinct from all retained-world rows because of \(S\). Complete every unused row arbitrarily. Assumption~\texttt{ass:complete-predecessor-functions} and \texttt{def:ordered-evaluation} then give a complete response system extending \(P_\alpha\) that satisfies the factual pin and \(\delta_b\).

From \(P_\beta\), choose a \(\beta\)-block containing indices \(j,\ell\) with \(b_j\neq b_\ell\). Those worlds have the same complete predecessor tuple at \(Y\), so \texttt{def:ordered-evaluation} forces
\[
 E(f,I_j)_Y=f_Y(x^{I_j}_{<Y})
 =f_Y(x^{I_\ell}_{<Y})=E(f,I_\ell)_Y
\]
for every complete-predecessor response system \(f\). It is therefore impossible to satisfy both required values in \(\delta_b\). The same legal future specification is feasible from one prefix and infeasible from the other, even though the response completion on the feasible side is quantified independently. Hence all \(B_h\) prefixes \(P_\alpha\) are pairwise residual-inequivalent, which proves \(\rho(h)\geq B_h\).

Combining the two inequalities yields \(\rho(h)=B_h\). Finally, \texttt{thm:single-conjunction-compiler} supplies the existing upper bound
\[
 B_h3^{(h-1)/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}).
\]
The lower-bound argument counts necessary exact residual states only. It does not lower-bound the time required to manipulate those states and does not quantify over other decision-diagram representations.
theorem.justification: This theorem certifies that complete-prefix equality is not only sufficient but worst-case state-minimal for the declared existential-support continuation interface.
theorem.gap: General knowledge-compilation methodology does not determine the causal residual quotient, and the inspected causal-order construction does not prove a \(\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) state frontier.
theorem.consumer: The compiler may use equality partitions as a canonical worst-case optimal state while retaining its existing \(B_h3^{(h-1)/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})\) upper bound.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Fix \(h\in\mathbb N_{+}\) and a normalized retained context set \(\mathcal H\) of cardinality \(h\). Two feasible normalized prefixes \(P\) and \(P'\) through the same layer are residual-equivalent if and only if, for every legal future pin specification \(\lambda\) and every terminal predecessor-normal conjunction \(\gamma^{\circ}\) produced by \(\mathsf N\) over the retained context system \(\mathcal H\),
\[
 \bigl[\text{there exists a complete-predecessor response system \(f\) extending \(P\) that accepts \((\lambda,\gamma^{\circ})\)}\bigr]
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \bigl[\text{there exists a complete-predecessor response system \(f'\) extending \(P'\) that accepts \((\lambda,\gamma^{\circ})\)}\bigr].
\]
Equivalently, the prefixes have the same attainable support of future retained-world value columns and terminal acceptance outcomes. The two existentially quantified completing response systems may differ; in particular, residual equivalence does not require a single concrete numerical response table to extend both prefixes. Define \(\rho(h)\) as the maximum, over finite ordered instances, normalized retained context systems of size \(h\), layers, and legal pin interfaces, of the number of residual-equivalence classes among feasible prefixes; equivalently, it is the minimum worst-case number of states of an exact online continuation summary. A summary is exact when equality of its state values implies residual equivalence; in particular, the complete-prefix partition \(\pi_i\) is exact when equality of \(\pi_i\) implies residual equivalence.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The former common-table wording coupled two prefixes to one concrete numerical response table and therefore retained labels that the partition compiler intentionally forgets. Already for \(h=1\), prefixes with predecessor tuples \((1,0)\) and \((1,1)\) have the same singleton partition, yet one shared \(Y\)-table with outputs zero and one distinguishes them by \(Y_I=0\). Under the intended support residual, each prefix may use its own completion, so both singleton prefixes admit an output-zero completion.

proposed.def: \(\mathcal H\) is exactly the set of distinct interventions occurring in \(\boldsymbol\gamma^{\circ}=\mathsf N(\boldsymbol\gamma)\). It is not augmented by the factual context \(\varnothing\) unless that context itself occurs in the normalized input.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The existing symbol text incorrectly adjoins the factual context, contrary to the retained-context construction in \(\texttt{def:query-normalizer}\) and to the required residual scope. The lower-bound query contains only nonfactual atoms, so its retained set must have cardinality exactly \(h\).

prose_updates.tldr: For standard finite order-compatible recursive structural causal models with arbitrary predecessor parent subsets and shared exogenous variation, sourced causal-order canonicalization permits sharp-bound optimization over a saturated all-predecessor response carrier. A deterministic normalizer extracts exactly the predecessor-only contexts retained by the query, and their complete-prefix equality partition is an exact continuation state. For the existential-support residual, in which each prefix may use its own response completion, this state is worst-case minimal: a binary selector construction realizes and pairwise separates all \(\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) partitions while the factual zero path remains outside the retained context set. Representative transitions give exact single-conjunction and joint-score compilers with exponential factors independent of alphabet cardinality, and sparse traceback attains the sharp observational cell-sum endpoints.

project_justification.gap: The closest exact order-only method proves canonical equivalence between parent-subset recursive models and complete all-predecessor response carriers, then enumerates completed response signatures before quotienting by observational and query evaluations. It does not establish predecessor normalization, complete-prefix equality as a local right congruence, or worst-case residual minimality under the correct existential-support continuation semantics.
project_justification.niche: Explicit unnested queries with few normalized retained contexts but many endogenous coordinates or large alphabets admit a smaller semantic state: later unrestricted response rows need only the equality pattern of retained-world complete prefixes. Residual equivalence compares attainable future supports and allows a different completing response system for each prefix, so it discards irrelevant numerical labels.
project_justification.fill: The project invokes the sourced canonical-carrier equivalence, proves deterministic normalization and equality-type continuation, derives complete representative transitions and explicit \(h\)- and \(r\)-dependent bounds, reconstructs sparse response systems, certifies sharp endpoints, and proves \(\rho(h)=\operatorname{Bell}(h)\). The lower bound uses \(h\) nonfactual contexts, binary subset selectors, and terminal conjunctions constant on one partition but inconsistent within a block of another. It is a state lower bound for the declared support residual, not a running-time or general decision-diagram lower bound.

prose_updates.related_work: Rossetto and Antonucci, in \emph{Partial Identification under Causal Orders by Linear Programming}, establish the order-only identified set and the equivalence permitting optimization over complete all-predecessor response signatures even when the standard recursive model has parent subsets. The present compiler takes that equivalence as its interface and tightens the query-specific construction for small \(h\); it does not redefine arbitrary recursive models as saturated. Halpern supplies finite recursive causal certificates and broad satisfiability hardness, but not a world-count continuation parameter. Ganian, Gr\"{u}ndel, and Wietheger study a different fixed-parameter satisfiability problem over inequalities on probability terms; no reduction or tightening is claimed here. Huber and coauthors compile fixed structural equations into arithmetic circuits for approximate causal-EM inner bounds, whereas this result quantifies exactly over mechanisms compatible with \(p\). Darwiche and Marquis supply general succinctness methodology but no causal residual theorem. The present \(\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) result is instead proved directly for existential feasibility supports, with independently quantified completions on the compared prefixes. Work on arbitrary graphs, fully specified mechanisms, and prescribed sparse graphs remains outside this claim.
prose_updates.interpretation: The equality partition forgets numerical prefix labels and retains exactly the cross-world coincidence information observable by a future unrestricted complete-predecessor response row. This interpretation requires existential support semantics: two prefixes are compared by whether each has some accepting completion, and those completions may be different. Requiring one concrete response table to extend both would retain numerical labels and would already split equivalent singleton partitions. The binary selector family shows that all \(\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) coincidence patterns can nevertheless affect a later causal conjunction. This is optimality for the declared online residual state, not a total-time lower bound or a claim about every compilation language.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The equality partition is insufficient when a sparse parent graph is prescribed as part of the optimization class, because a later mechanism may observe equality only on its actual parent coordinates rather than on complete prefixes. The standard order-compatible target allows parent subsets, but its sharp-bound optimization uses the sourced saturated canonical carrier; that equivalence does not license the same quotient after conditioning on a prescribed sparse graph. The residual lower bound is scoped to existential feasibility of future pins and terminal normalized conjunctions. It neither couples compared prefixes to one response table nor implies an \(h\log h\) time lower bound or a lower bound for all reduced multi-valued decision diagrams. Dense input reading, explicit unnesting, and rational bit complexity are charged; prescribed sparse graphs, independence restrictions, cycles, succinct nested syntax, and experimental-table constraints are excluded.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The sourced canonical equivalence from standard order-compatible parent-subset models to the saturated all-predecessor response carrier is used only as an interface. The normalization, continuation, representative bounds, joint truth-state compiler, sparse reconstruction, cellwise attainment, false-bit criterion, and numeric-history separation are internal results. The residual theorem proves exactly \(\rho(h)=\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) for existential continuation supports using \(h\) nonfactual retained contexts and a separate factual zero path. Its witness completions may differ between prefixes; no common numerical response-table suffix is asserted. No running-time lower bound, universal decision-diagram lower bound, prescribed-sparse-graph extension, factorized-exogenous extension, or direct nested-syntax extension is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: Complete-prefix equality is both sufficient and worst-case minimal for exact existential-support continuation.
statement_notes.gap: Neither general knowledge-compilation results nor the sourced causal-order construction provide this causal Myhill--Nerode characterization.
statement_notes.consumer: The result certifies the \(B_h\) state factor used by the single-conjunction compiler while expressly leaving time complexity and other representation classes open.
